note.text: The first bend repeatedly caught the trailer rear-right, while sustained leftward turning swept the tractor front-right into the rail. Starting the turn earlier cleared the first trailer contact point but did not clear the full bend; straightening there was also too early. Watch both ends and use the rails to judge the path, not hitch angle alone. Pulling forward with centered wheels was blocked at the front-right rail; a gentle left turn freed it. The tractor’s long rear overhang makes front swing significant.

notes_in.text: The left bend repeatedly caught the trailer's left corners. The best attempt turned gradually early, increased the angle near the bend, then followed the trailer; it reached farther but still hit the rear-left rail. Watch camera clearance continuously and adjust before the corner closes in, rather than relying on progress alone. Avoid repeated pull-ups and excessive articulation: the long trailer responds slowly, and sharp early turns trap its front corner. Leave room and time to straighten into the bay.

note.text: The rear-left corner repeatedly struck the inside rail near the bend; late corrections and simply holding the trailer straight did not clear it. A stronger early rightward shift then caught the front-left corner, so watch both ends of the trailer and the cab, using mirrors as well as the camera. Plan the approach well before the bend, make gradual position changes, and follow the trailer early. This long trailer responds slowly, so allow plenty of distance for each correction and avoid repeated pull-ups.
